themes.name: The Question of Monstrosity
themes.description: Each monster encounter illuminates a different facet of the question: What makes a monster?
examples: Elder Gransel: Humans who harm children while cloaked in respectability.
Werefolk: Monsters can be falsely accused. The label is often a political tool.
Gremlins: Some creatures are simply animals. Not evil, just wild.
Wendigo: True evil exists. Some monsters chose their path.
Abusive parents, corrupt clergy, the Archbishop: Monstrosity is not limited to supernatural beings.
Cordelia: A monster who rejected monstrous ideology. Nature does not define choices.

themes.name: Institutional Corruption vs. Personal Faith
themes.description: Both protagonists are exiles from corrupt institutions. The story examines different responses.

positions.Elijah: Believes in reform from within, or at least personal integrity while serving. Faith in God, not in the Church, but works through Church structures.
positions.Cordelia: Believes in escape. When the institution fails, you leave. You do not reform it; you survive it.

themes.resolution: The story does not resolve which approach is correct. Both pay a price.

themes.name: Exile as Identity
themes.description: Both protagonists are exiles. Elijah was cast out for righteousness. Cordelia left before she was forced to participate in evil. Their parallel histories reveal different responses to institutional failure.
themes.theParallel: They are the same. Both chose conscience over belonging. Both paid the price of exile. Both found meaning in helping others. And yet one will judge the other.

themes.name: Small Acts vs. Systemic Change
themes.description: Elijah found meaning in hunting: direct action, saving one person at a time. Cordelia saved a handful of children. Neither changed the corrupt systems.
themes.question: Do these small acts matter? Or do they simply make broken systems tolerable by providing exceptions that prevent total collapse?
themes.resolution: No answer is given. The children are safe. Cordelia will be tried. Elijah's faith is wounded. The Archbishop still holds power. The world is not fixed.
